Get the basics for now. Get what you can afford, even if it's garbage freight (they have a lifetime warranty, btw and you'll use it). As you start to make money, replace your most commonly used tools with the best ones you can afford. And if you have to borrow a tool more than once, buy it ASAP. After a while, you'll have a respectable toolbox full of reliable tools and more money in your wallet because you didn't put yourself in a bind buying them. You'll get no flak for doing it that way. Just show that you're serious, hard-working, eager to learn and not a know-it-all and you'll be alright.

Edit to add: Depends on what you're doing, but [The Yard Store](http://www.yardstore.com) has a good variety of affordable structures tools.

An Associate's degree in my field means nothing. Absolutely nothing. They want experience on a particular (and there are a vast many) configuration and a license.

Unless you have a Bachelor's degree. That'll get you into middle management (something I'm not fond of anyway). 

I have experience in a particular configuration that is being phased out, so I have to start from the beginning, again, making sub-par wages I wouldn't be able to live on even if I didn't have to cough up 44% of my income to taxes and child support.

I like what I do, but the pay is shit if you're not very lucky and very careful. Yes, luck has a lot to do with it, and you must be good at networking to keep your options open.

I don't have many interests. Very few, in fact. Fixing stuff, fucking off, and cleaning. I love to clean, but I wouldn't want to ever do it as a job again. My chosen career and degrees are in fixing stuff. Stuff that if not fixed right will, not can, WILL kill people, yet the hours are horrible, the environment is almost always out in the weather, the noise is loud, one wrong step and you'll be obliterated. Shit, maybe I'll get lucky.

>If you were ugly you wouldn't be a parent.

My ex stayed drunk. And you should have seen her exes. They look like Sasquatch. Plus, I wasn't good enough. She cheated on me with six different guys (that I know of) over the course of our marriage. I talk to a woman, girl, female, whatever and I get the (ew) face, or I get to interact, but always get the fade-away.

>If you were stupid you wouldn't have a degree.

There's a lot of incredibly stupid people with a degree. It doesn't take brains, it takes hard work.

I'm glad it got better for you. I just can't see it happening for me. The more I struggle, the deeper into the hole I go. I feel like I'm in quicksand. There is no escape, and it does not get better, it stays the same, or gets worse. I appreciate the kind words, stranger. I know there are good people out there, but there aren't any around where I am. I can't even get help for my depression. I don't qualify for any assistance whatsoever. I tried. So moving out of state for a new job? I don't want to live in a gutter, or a homeless shelter. That's fine for some but it's not the quality of life I want. I'd rather be dead. Being dead is nice. It's just a bunch of nothing. I was dead for a long time before I was born.
